useCases.name: RegisterModelArtifact

businessRules.text:
Registering a model artifact is a port-backed operation over a file already persisted by FileUpload. modelName is the human-readable artifact name shown to operators. modelPlugin is the strict runtime-engine model plugin code used to select DenseNet, ResNet, UNet, or other execution implementations. modelVersion identifies the business version under that display name, and modelDescription captures the business purpose, training background, applicable scenarios, or limitations that operators need when selecting the model. The pair must be unique. modelId remains the system identity for one imported or trained artifact version. sourceType distinguishes externally uploaded artifacts from artifacts produced by federated training. fileId identifies the shared FileUpload record; ModelRepository does not create a second physical copy or a second storage subsystem. The adapter resolves FileUpload metadata and content URI, validates the model format, records digest and size, and marks the file reference after registration. modelArtifactUri remains the authenticated FileUpload content URI.

useCases.name: SelectTrainingRoundParticipants

businessRules.text: Each training round starts from a runtime snapshot selected by domain policy. Selection first verifies that the federation has joined organizations and that those organizations have dataset metadata for the training configuration's exact feature schema with both schema and label compatibility confirmed. Only then can an active runtime identity with the same organization and runtime identity be paired with that dataset. One deterministic dataset is selected per runtime for a round snapshot. When personalization is enabled, the selected participant also carries the stable personalization target and optional cohort/profile identity used by execution planning and personalized artifact lineage. Runtimes that become ready after a round has begun cannot join that round, but they can be selected for a later round when policy allows dynamic round snapshots. If federation membership, compatible dataset evidence, runtime identity matching, personalization capability matching, or quorum validation fails, the system records a failed participant selection event with a stage-specific reason so the operator can fix readiness and retry selection.

useCases.name: StartRoundExecution

businessRules.text:
Starting a round execution is responsible for launching the local runtime engine on demand for this participant round, not for calling a pre-existing always-on engine. The adapter prepares the local training workspace and configuration, starts the matching runtime engine service, process, or container, submits the local model training job to that engine, and records the created runtimeEngineJobId. The port records exactly one outcome: RoundExecutionStarted when the runtime engine is running and the training job has been accepted, or RoundExecutionStartFailed when environment preparation, engine startup, model loading, personalized base loading, resource allocation, or training job submission fails.
Runtime engine model selection must come from the participant execution plan baseModelPlugin snapshot. Runtime agents must not decide the model plugin from model display names, registry references, or local environment variables because the selected model is platform training configuration data.
Runtime engine image selection must come from the participant execution plan RuntimeEngineProfile snapshot. Runtime-agent local configuration is only a fallback for legacy plans that do not carry a runtimeEngineImage.
When personalization is enabled, StartRoundExecution must pass the personalization mode, target identity, artifact policy, and optional personalized base model artifact to the runtime engine. The runtime engine may return both a global model update and a personalized artifact, but only the global update participates in platform aggregation.
When secureAggregationRequired is true, StartRoundExecution must pass encryptionScheme, publicKeyVersion, publicKeyRef, and encryptedParameterScale to the runtime engine so the local model update is encrypted inside the participant runtime boundary before any update artifact is reported to the platform.
